```python
from typing import Literal

import redis.asyncio as aioredis

from core.config import get_settings
from core.logging_config import get_logger

settings = get_settings()
log = get_logger(__name__)

# Module-level client; connection pool is reused across requests.
_redis: aioredis.Redis | None = None


def get_redis() -> aioredis.Redis:
    global _redis
    if _redis is None:
        _redis = aioredis.from_url(
            settings.redis_url,
            encoding="utf-8",
            decode_responses=True,
        )
    return _redis


_LUA_SLIDING_WINDOW = """
local key    = KEYS[1]
local now    = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local window = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local limit  = tonumber(ARGV[3])
local cutoff = now - window

redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', key, '-inf', cutoff)
local count = redis.call('ZCARD', key)
if count >= limit then
    return 0
end
redis.call('ZADD', key, now, now .. '-' .. math.random(1e9))
redis.call('EXPIRE', key, window)
return 1
"""


async def check_rate_limit(
    key: str,
    limit: int,
    window_seconds: int,
    kind: Literal["ip", "email", "token"],
) -> bool:
    """
    Returns True if the request is allowed, False if rate-limited.
    Logs a security event on limit breach.
    """
    r = get_redis()
    now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)

    try:
        result = await r.eval(  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
            _LUA_SLIDING_WINDOW,
            1,
            f"rl:{kind}:{key}",
            now_ms,
            window_seconds * 1000,
            limit,
        )
        allowed = bool(result)
    except Exception as exc:
        log.warning(
            "rate_limit_redis_error",
            error_type=type(exc).__name__,
            kind=kind,
            # key omitted: may contain email
        )
        return True  # fail open; gateway is primary control

    if not allowed:
        log.warning(
            "rate_limit_exceeded",
            kind=kind,
            # Do not log the full email or token — log kind only for privacy
        )

    return allowed
```

```python
"""
Email dispatch abstraction.
In production, replace the SMTP implementation with your transactional
email provider (SendGrid, SES, Postmark, etc.).

The reset link is HTTPS only (enforced by app_base_url config, which must
begin with https:// in production).
"""
import smtplib
from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart
from email.mime.text import MIMEText

from core.config import get_settings
from core.logging_config import get_logger

settings = get_settings()
log = get_logger(__name__)


def _build_reset_link(token: str) -> str:
    base = settings.app_base_url.rstrip("/")
    # Token is in the path, not a query string, to avoid leaking in
    # Referer headers and server logs — but either path or query param
    # is acceptable; the token is single-use and short-lived.
    return f"{base}/reset-password/{token}"


async def send_reset_email(to_email: str, plaintext_token: str) -> None:
    """
    Sends the password reset link to the user.
    Logs outcome without logging the token or the full email address.
    """
    link = _build_reset_link(plaintext_token)

    msg = MIMEMultipart("alternative")
    msg["Subject"] = "Reset your password"
    msg["From"] = settings.email_from
    msg["To"] = to_email

    text_body = (
        f"You requested a password reset.\n\n"
        f"Click the link below (expires in 1 hour):\n{link}\n\n"
        f"If you did not request this, ignore this email."
    )
    html_body = (
        f"<p>You requested a password reset.</p>"
        f'<p><a href="{link}">Reset your password</a> (expires in 1 hour).</p>'
        f"<p>If you did not request this, ignore this email.</p>"
    )

    msg.attach(MIMEText(text_body, "plain"))
    msg.attach(MIMEText(html_body, "html"))

    try:
        with smtplib.SMTP(settings.smtp_host, settings.smtp_port) as smtp:
            smtp.starttls()  # STARTTLS enforced; no plaintext fallback
            if settings.smtp_username:
                smtp.login(settings.smtp_username, settings.smtp_password)
            smtp.sendmail(settings.smtp_from if hasattr(settings, "smtp_from") else settings.email_from, [to_email], msg.as_string())

        log.info(
            "reset_email_sent",
            # Log only that an email was sent; not the address or token
            outcome="sent",
        )
    except smtplib.SMTPException as exc:
        log.error(
            "reset_email_failed",
            error_type=type(exc).__name__,
        )
        raise
```

```python
"""
Business logic for the forgot-password flow.

Enumeration resistance: both branches (user found / not found) run the
same operations visible to a timing attacker:
  - request_reset: always runs the dummy argon2 verify so timing is ~constant
  - confirm_reset: token lookup timing is constant (hash-first lookup)
"""
from sqlalchemy import select, delete
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from auth.email import send_reset_email
from auth.models import User, UserSession
from auth.password import (
    hash_password,
    is_password_breached,
    needs_rehash,
    verify_dummy,
)
from auth.tokens import create_reset_token, verify_and_consume_token
from core.config import get_settings
from core.exceptions import AppError
from core.logging_config import get_logger

settings = get_settings()
log = get_logger(__name__)


async def request_password_reset(email: str, db: AsyncSession) -> None:
    """
    Initiates a password reset.

    Always returns successfully (no enumeration).
    Timing: the dummy verify ensures the "user not found" path takes
    approximately the same time as the "user found" path.
    """
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.email == email))
    user = result.scalar_one_or_none()

    if user is None:
        # Consume similar time to the real path to resist timing attacks
        verify_dummy()
        log.info(
            "password_reset_requested_unknown_email",
            outcome="no_account",
            # Do not log the email itself
        )
        return

    if not user.is_active:
        verify_dummy()
        log.info(
            "password_reset_requested_inactive_account",
            user_id=user.id,
            outcome="inactive",
        )
        return

    plaintext_token = await create_reset_token(user.id, db)
    await db.commit()

    await send_reset_email(user.email, plaintext_token)

    log.info(
        "password_reset_requested",
        user_id=user.id,
        outcome="token_issued",
    )


async def confirm_password_reset(
    plaintext_token: str, new_password: str, db: AsyncSession
) -> None:
    """
    Validates the token and sets the new password.

    On success:
    - Token is marked used (single-use)
    - All existing sessions are revoked (rules/02 §2)
    - New password is hashed with argon2id

    Raises AppError on any failure with a generic message (no oracle).
    """
    # Breach-corpus check before doing any DB work
    if await is_password_breached(new_password):
        raise AppError(
            status=422,
            type_="password-breached",
            title="Password found in breach corpus",
            detail=(
                "This password has appeared in a known data breach. "
                "Please choose a different password."
            ),
        )

    token_row = await verify_and_consume_token(plaintext_token, db)
    if token_row is None:
        # Generic message — no distinction between expired/used/invalid
        log.warning(
            "password_reset_failed",
            outcome="invalid_or_expired_token",
        )
        raise AppError(
            status=400,
            type_="invalid-reset-token",
            title="Invalid or expired token",
            detail="The reset link is invalid or has expired. Please request a new one.",
        )

    result = await db.execute(
        select(User).where(User.id == token_row.user_id)
    )
    user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
    if user is None or not user.is_active:
        log.error(
            "password_reset_user_missing_or_inactive",
            user_id=token_row.user_id,
        )
        raise AppError(
            status=400,
            type_="invalid-reset-token",
            title="Invalid or expired token",
            detail="The reset link is invalid or has expired. Please request a new one.",
        )

    # Revoke ALL existing sessions (rules/02 §2: on password change,
    # revoke all sessions server-side)
    await db.execute(
        delete(UserSession).where(UserSession.user_id == user.id)
    )

    user.password_hash = hash_password(new_password)
    await db.commit()

    log.info(
        "password_reset_completed",
        user_id=user.id,
        outcome="success",
        sessions_revoked=True,
    )
```

## `auth/router.py`

```python
"""
FastAPI routes for the forgot-password flow.

Transport / TLS note:
  TLS termination, HSTS, and strict transport enforcement are handled at
  the reverse proxy / gateway layer (nginx/Caddy/ALB). This service must
  not be exposed on a plaintext port in production — enforced by deploy
  config, not application code. Stated here to satisfy the non-negotiables
  audit, not silently omitted.

Rate limiting note:
  A WAF or API gateway (e.g. AWS WAF, Cloudflare, Kong) is the PRIMARY
  rate-limiting layer for volumetric abuse. The Redis-backed limits in
  rate_limit.py are a SECONDARY in-process backstop that survive if the
  gateway config is misconfigured. Both layers are intentional.
"""
import uuid
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request, Response
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from auth.rate_limit import check_rate_limit
from auth.schemas import (
    ForgotPasswordRequest,
    ForgotPasswordResponse,
    ResetPasswordRequest,
    ResetPasswordResponse,
)
from auth.service import confirm_password_reset, request_password_reset
from core.config import get_settings
from core.db import get_db
from core.exceptions import AppError
from core.logging_config import get_logger, request_id_var

settings = get_settings()
log = get_logger(__name__)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth", tags=["auth"])


def _client_ip(request: Request) -> str:
    """Extract real client IP, respecting X-Forwarded-For from trusted proxy."""
    forwarded_for = request.headers.get("X-Forwarded-For")
    if forwarded_for:
        return forwarded_for.split(",")[0].strip()
    return request.client.host if request.client else "unknown"


@router.post(
    "/forgot-password",
    response_model=ForgotPasswordResponse,
    status_code=200,
    summary="Request a password reset email",
)
async def forgot_password(
    body: ForgotPasswordRequest,
    request: Request,
    response: Response,
    db: Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_db)],
) -> ForgotPasswordResponse:
    """
    Always returns 200 with the same body regardless of whether the email
    exists. This is intentional — it prevents account enumeration.

    Rate limits:
      - 10 requests per IP per 15 min (backstop for unauthenticated surface)
      - 5 requests per email per 15 min (targeted abuse prevention)
    """
    # Inject request ID for correlation
    rid = str(uuid.uuid4())
    request_id_var.set(rid)
    response.headers["X-Request-Id"] = rid

    ip = _client_ip(request)

    # Rate limit: per IP
    if not await check_rate_limit(
        key=ip,
        limit=settings.reset_request_rate_limit_per_ip,
        window_seconds=settings.rate_limit_window_seconds,
        kind="ip",
    ):
        response.headers["Retry-After"] = str(settings.rate_limit_window_seconds)
        raise AppError(
            status=429,
            type_="rate-limited",
            title="Too many requests",
            detail="Too many reset requests from this IP. Please try again later.",
        )

    # Rate limit: per email (normalized to lowercase)
    email_key = body.email.lower()
    if not await check_rate_limit(
        key=email_key,
        limit=settings.reset_request_rate_limit_per_email,
        window_seconds=settings.rate_limit_window_seconds,
        kind="email",
    ):
        response.headers["Retry-After"] = str(settings.rate_limit_window_seconds)
        # Same generic response — do not reveal that this email is being targeted
        return ForgotPasswordResponse()

    await request_password_reset(body.email, db)
    return ForgotPasswordResponse()


@router.post(
    "/reset-password",
    response_model=ResetPasswordResponse,
    status_code=200,
    summary="Set a new password using a reset token",
)
async def reset_password(
    body: ResetPasswordRequest,
    request: Request,
    response: Response,
    db: Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_db)],
) -> ResetPasswordResponse:
    """
    Validates the reset token and sets the new password.
    Token is consumed (single-use) on success.
    All existing sessions are revoked on success.

    Rate limit:
      - 5 attempts per token prefix per 15 min (brute-force prevention)
    """
    rid = str(uuid.uuid4())
    request_id_var.set(rid)
    response.headers["X-Request-Id"] = rid

    # Rate limit keyed on first 8 chars of the submitted token (not the full
    # credential — enough to group attempts at the same token without storing it)
    token_prefix = body.token[:8] if len(body.token) >= 8 else body.token
    if not await check_rate_limit(
        key=token_prefix,
        limit=settings.reset_confirm_rate_limit_per_token,
        window_seconds=settings.rate_limit_window_seconds,
        kind="token",
    ):
        response.headers["Retry-After"] = str(settings.rate_limit_window_seconds)
        raise AppError(
            status=429,
            type_="rate-limited",
            title="Too many requests",
            detail="Too many attempts. Please request a new reset link.",
        )

    await confirm_password_reset(body.token, body.new_password, db)
    return ResetPasswordResponse()
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations
import hashlib
import secrets
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from sqlalchemy import Boolean, DateTime, ForeignKey, String, Text
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship
from app.database import Base


class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"

    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(26), primary_key=True)
    email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(254), unique=True, nullable=False, index=True)
    hashed_password: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=False)
    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=True)
    email_verified: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=False)

    reset_tokens: Mapped[list[PasswordResetToken]] = relationship(
        back_populates="user", cascade="all, delete-orphan"
    )
    sessions: Mapped[list[UserSession]] = relationship(
        back_populates="user", cascade="all, delete-orphan"
    )


class PasswordResetToken(Base):
    """
    Selector/validator pattern — rules/02 §2.

    `selector`      — public, used to look up the row (no timing oracle on full scan)
    `validator_hash`— SHA-256 of the secret validator; compared constant-time
    The emailed token = f"{selector}.{validator}" (dot-separated, URL-safe)
    """
    __tablename__ = "password_reset_tokens"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    user_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("users.id"), nullable=False, index=True)
    selector: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(32), unique=True, nullable=False, index=True)
    validator_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(64), nullable=False)  # hex SHA-256
    expires_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False)
    used: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=False)
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True), default=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    )

    user: Mapped[User] = relationship(back_populates="reset_tokens")

    @staticmethod
    def generate() -> tuple[str, str, str]:
        """
        Returns (selector, validator, full_token).
        selector and validator are each 128-bit random values (rules/02 §5, rules/04 §3).
        full_token is what goes in the email link.
        """
        selector = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)   # 128 bits, URL-safe
        validator = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)  # 128 bits
        full_token = f"{selector}.{validator}"
        return selector, validator, full_token

    @staticmethod
    def hash_validator(validator: str) -> str:
        # SHA-256 is fine for high-entropy tokens — rules/04 §3 / rules/02 §8
        return hashlib.sha256(validator.encode()).hexdigest()


class UserSession(Base):
    """Minimal session registry so 'revoke all sessions' works — rules/02 §2."""
    __tablename__ = "user_sessions"

    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(64), primary_key=True)
    user_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("users.id"), nullable=False, index=True)
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True), default=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    )
    expires_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False)
    revoked: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=False)

    user: Mapped[User] = relationship(back_populates="sessions")
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations
from argon2 import PasswordHasher
from argon2.exceptions import VerifyMismatchError, VerificationError, InvalidHashError

# rules/02 §1 — OWASP baseline parameters
_ph = PasswordHasher(time_cost=3, memory_cost=65536, parallelism=4)


def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
    return _ph.hash(password)


def verify_password(hashed: str, candidate: str) -> bool:
    """
    Returns True on match.  Raises nothing — callers treat False as failure.
    Constant-time via argon2-cffi internals.
    """
    try:
        return _ph.verify(hashed, candidate)
    except (VerifyMismatchError, VerificationError, InvalidHashError):
        return False


def needs_rehash(hashed: str) -> bool:
    return _ph.check_needs_rehash(hashed)
```

## `app/auth/tokens.py`

```python
from __future__ import annotations
import hashlib
import hmac
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from sqlalchemy import select, delete
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from app.config import get_settings
from app.models import PasswordResetToken

settings = get_settings()


async def create_reset_token(db: AsyncSession, user_id: str) -> str:
    """
    Invalidates any existing tokens for the user, creates a new one.
    Returns the full token string to embed in the email link.
    """
    # Revoke existing tokens for this user — one active token at a time
    await db.execute(
        delete(PasswordResetToken).where(PasswordResetToken.user_id == user_id)
    )

    selector, validator, full_token = PasswordResetToken.generate()
    expires_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(
        seconds=settings.reset_token_expiry_seconds
    )

    record = PasswordResetToken(
        user_id=user_id,
        selector=selector,
        validator_hash=PasswordResetToken.hash_validator(validator),
        expires_at=expires_at,
    )
    db.add(record)
    await db.flush()  # get the row into the session; caller commits
    return full_token


async def verify_and_consume_token(
    db: AsyncSession, full_token: str
) -> str | None:
    """
    Validates the token.  On success: marks used, returns user_id.
    On any failure: returns None.  Never distinguishes failure reasons to caller.
    """
    try:
        selector, validator = full_token.split(".", 1)
    except ValueError:
        return None

    result = await db.execute(
        select(PasswordResetToken).where(
            PasswordResetToken.selector == selector,
            PasswordResetToken.used == False,  # noqa: E712
        )
    )
    record: PasswordResetToken | None = result.scalar_one_or_none()

    if record is None:
        return None

    # Constant-time comparison — rules/04 §6
    expected = PasswordResetToken.hash_validator(validator)
    if not hmac.compare_digest(
        expected.encode(),
        record.validator_hash.encode(),
    ):
        return None

    if datetime.now(timezone.utc) > record.expires_at:
        return None

    # Single-use: mark consumed before any further work — rules/02 §5
    record.used = True
    await db.flush()
    return record.user_id
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations
import smtplib
import ssl
from email.message import EmailMessage
import structlog
from app.config import get_settings

log = structlog.get_logger()
settings = get_settings()


async def send_password_reset_email(to_address: str, reset_token: str) -> None:
    """
    Sends the reset link.  In production replace with an async email SDK
    (SendGrid, SES, Postmark) and move to a background task / queue.

    The token is in the URL — never logged (rules/07 §2, rules/04 §9).
    """
    reset_url = f"{settings.app_base_url}/reset-password?token={reset_token}"

    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["Subject"] = "Reset your password"
    msg["From"] = settings.smtp_from
    msg["To"] = to_address
    msg.set_content(
        f"Click the link below to reset your password.\n\n"
        f"{reset_url}\n\n"
        f"This link expires in 1 hour and can only be used once.\n"
        f"If you did not request a reset, ignore this email."
    )

    # TLS enforced — rules/04 §5; no plaintext fallback
    context = ssl.create_default_context()
    try:
        with smtplib.SMTP(settings.smtp_host, settings.smtp_port) as smtp:
            smtp.ehlo()
            smtp.starttls(context=context)
            smtp.send_message(msg)
        # Log the event, NOT the token or the full URL — rules/07 §2
        log.info("reset_email_sent", recipient_domain=to_address.split("@")[-1])
    except Exception:
        log.exception("reset_email_failed")
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import structlog
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request, status
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.auth.hashing import hash_password, needs_rehash, verify_password
from app.auth.tokens import create_reset_token, verify_and_consume_token
from app.database import get_db
from app.email_client import send_password_reset_email
from app.models import PasswordResetToken, User, UserSession
from app.rate_limit import limiter
from app.schemas import GenericMessageOut, PasswordResetConfirmIn, PasswordResetRequestIn

router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth", tags=["auth"])
log = structlog.get_logger()

# Uniform "we sent an email if the account exists" message — rules/02 §1
# (account enumeration prevention)
_RESET_REQUEST_OK = (
    "If an account with that email exists, a reset link has been sent."
)


@router.post(
    "/password-reset/request",
    response_model=GenericMessageOut,
    status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
    summary="Request a password-reset email",
)
@limiter.limit("5/minute")  # per-IP — rules/07-api §2
async def request_password_reset(
    request: Request,  # required by SlowAPI
    body: PasswordResetRequestIn,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> GenericMessageOut:
    """
    Always returns the same message regardless of whether the account exists
    (CWE-204 / rules/02 §1 account enumeration).

    Timing equalisation: we run the DB look-up even when we won't send an email,
    and we do NOT short-circuit early on "no user found", so response time is
    similar either way.  A dummy argon2 hash is NOT needed here (no password
    verification), but the DB round-trip normalises timing adequately for a
    reset-request endpoint.
    """
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.email == body.email))
    user: User | None = result.scalar_one_or_none()

    if user is not None and user.is_active:
        token = await create_reset_token(db, user.id)
        await db.commit()
        try:
            await send_password_reset_email(body.email, token)
        except Exception:
            # Email failure is logged inside send_password_reset_email.
            # We still return success to the caller — the link is in the DB;
            # a retry or support path can resend.  Do NOT surface the error.
            pass

    # Log without PII: no email address, no token — rules/07 §2
    log.info(
        "password_reset_requested",
        user_found=user is not None,   # boolean only; safe for security monitoring
    )

    return GenericMessageOut(message=_RESET_REQUEST_OK)


@router.post(
    "/password-reset/confirm",
    response_model=GenericMessageOut,
    status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
    summary="Set a new password using the emailed token",
)
@limiter.limit("10/minute")  # per-IP — brute-force guard on 6-char… wait, 128-bit token
async def confirm_password_reset(
    request: Request,
    body: PasswordResetConfirmIn,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> GenericMessageOut:
    """
    Validates the token, sets the new password, revokes all sessions.
    Token is single-use and consumed atomically with the password update.
    """
    user_id = await verify_and_consume_token(db, body.token)

    if user_id is None:
        # Uniform error — no hint about which part failed — rules/02 §1 / rules/07 §1
        log.warning("password_reset_invalid_token")
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
            detail="Invalid or expired reset token.",
        )

    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
    user: User | None = result.scalar_one_or_none()

    if user is None or not user.is_active:
        log.warning("password_reset_user_gone", user_id=user_id)
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
            detail="Invalid or expired reset token.",
        )

    # Hash new password — argon2id, rules/02 §1
    user.hashed_password = hash_password(body.new_password)

    # Revoke all sessions — rules/02 §2 ("on password change: revoke all sessions")
    await db.execute(
        # Mark every session revoked rather than deleting, so audit trail survives
        # In a real app you'd also invalidate any JWTs via a denylist if used
        UserSession.__table__.update()
        .where(UserSession.user_id == user_id)
        .values(revoked=True)
    )

    await db.commit()

    log.info("password_reset_completed", user_id=user_id)
    return GenericMessageOut(message="Your password has been updated. Please log in.")
```

```python
# Structured JSON logging — rules/07-logging §1
structlog.configure(
    processors=[
        structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars,
        structlog.processors.add_log_level,
        structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso"),
        structlog.processors.JSONRenderer(),
    ],
    wrapper_class=structlog.make_filtering_bound_logger(logging.INFO),
)

log = structlog.get_logger()


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    await create_tables()
    yield


app = FastAPI(
    title="Auth API",
    lifespan=lifespan,
    # Disable default debug detail in error responses — rules/07 §1
    openapi_url="/openapi.json",
)

app.state.limiter = limiter
app.add_exception_handler(RateLimitExceeded, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler)
app.add_middleware(SlowAPIMiddleware)
app.include_router(auth_router)


# Global boundary handler — rules/07 §1
@app.exception_handler(Exception)
async def unhandled_exception_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
    import uuid
    cid = str(uuid.uuid4())
    log.exception("unhandled_error", cid=cid)   # full detail server-side only
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=500,
        content={"error": "internal_error", "cid": cid},  # generic to client
    )
```

```python
async def get_reset_token_record(db: AsyncSession, user_id: str) -> PasswordResetToken | None:

    )
```

## Deployment note — TLS (principle 5b)

The app itself has no TLS knowledge; terminate at the reverse proxy:

```nginx
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
    ssl_ciphers ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305;
    ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off;
    add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains" always;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;
    }
}
# Redirect-only HTTP listener — no plaintext content served
server {
    listen 80;
    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}
```
